transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start off, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

I’m here because the clinic doctor was concerned about how little I’ve been eating. Most days it’s just coffee in the morning, maybe a few bites of something between jobs, and a small dinner if I’m not too busy with paperwork.
When you're eating less like this, is it because you're worried about your weight or how your body looks, or is it more that you just don't have time or don't feel hungry?

It’s more worry about gaining weight. If I eat something heavy, like pizza or a big sandwich, I get panicky that I’ll wake up bigger and slower, and then I won’t be able to move around ladders and rooms the way I need to for work.
Can you tell me your current height and weight, and how much weight you've lost over the past few months?

I don’t know the exact numbers offhand. My work pants are hanging pretty loose now, and people at job sites keep saying I look too thin. I just think I’ve leaned out from being on my feet all day, though.
When you look in the mirror or think about your body, do you feel like you're still too big or need to lose more weight, even though others say you look thin?
I mean, I don’t see it as some emergency like everyone else does. I just feel like I’m being disciplined and busy with work, and people are making a bigger deal out of my weight than it needs to be.
Can you tell me your current height and weight, even approximate numbers from a recent doctor's visit or scale?

I don’t have a number from a recent scale. I just know my work pants are pretty loose now, and people on the job keep telling me I look too thin. I’ve mostly thought it was from being on my feet all day.
Would you be willing to step on a scale right now so we can get an accurate current weight and height?
I’d rather not right now. My pants are definitely looser, but I’ve figured that’s just from being on my feet at work all day.
Have you ever had episodes where you eat a large amount of food and then feel you need to make up for it—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising intensely?
I’m not really sure what counts as a large amount. I haven’t noticed doing anything like that.
Have you noticed any changes in your menstrual cycle, such as periods becoming irregular or stopping altogether, since you started eating less?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really been keeping track closely enough to notice a pattern.
Even without a scale, can you give me your best guess at what you weigh now compared to what you weighed a few months ago before you started eating less?
I don’t really know a number. My work pants are hanging pretty loose now, and people at job sites have said I look too thin. But I think I’ve just leaned out from being on my feet all day.
Have you noticed feeling unusually cold, dizzy, lightheaded, or fatigued lately?
I haven’t really noticed anything unusual like that. I get tired after work sometimes, but I figured that was normal.
Do you happen to know your weight from any recent record—like a driver's license, work physical, or doctor's visit within the past year—that we could use to compare with how you look now?
I don’t have a recent number, no. I just know my work pants are pretty loose now, and people keep saying I look too thin. I think it’s mostly from being on my feet all day, though.
About how many pant or waist sizes have you dropped since your clothes started feeling loose?
I’m not sure how many sizes. I haven’t really kept track. I just know the pants I wear for work are hanging loose on me now.
Have you or others noticed your ribs, collarbones, or bones in your face becoming more visible or prominent than before?
People have said I look too thin lately. My work pants are hanging pretty loose, but I honestly think I’ve just leaned out from being on my feet all day.
Can you tell me the specific waist size printed on the pants you wear now, and compare it to the size you used to wear before you started eating less?

I don’t know the actual waist size, honestly. I just know the work pants I wear now hang pretty loose on me. People at job sites say I look too thin, but I think I’ve mostly just leaned out from being on my feet all day.
Even without an exact scale reading, can you give me your best estimate of how many pounds you think you've lost over the past few months?

I really couldn’t put a number on it. I don’t weigh myself. I just know my work pants are a lot looser, and people at job sites keep saying I look too thin. But I figured I’ve just leaned out from being on my feet all day.
Even if you don't know your current weight, could you tell me your height so I can get a sense of your build?

I’m not sure of my exact height. I just know my work pants are hanging really loose now, and people at job sites say I look too thin. I’ve thought of it more as leaning out from being on my feet all day.
Has any doctor, nurse, or other healthcare provider ever told you that your weight is below a healthy range for your height?
No, nobody’s actually told me that. They’ve commented that I look too thin, and my pants are loose, but I figured it was just from being on my feet working all day.

I understand you'd rather not right now, but given the health concerns here, I'd like to do a quick height and weight check as part of your physical exam today—would you be willing to do that as part of this visit?
I’d rather not do that today. My pants are loose, sure, and people say I look thin, but I really think I’ve just leaned out from being on my feet at work all day.
Would you be willing to step on the scale if we keep the number hidden from you, just so I can document it in your chart?
I’d still rather not. I know my pants are hanging loose and people keep saying I look too thin, but I think it’s mostly from being on my feet working all day.
Have you noticed any change in your physical strength or stamina at work—like trouble climbing ladders, carrying equipment, or keeping up with tasks you used to do easily?

I’m still showing up for work and class. It’s more that I’ve been avoiding lunches with coworkers or study meetups—it’s easier to keep my routine the way I want it and not have people commenting on what I’m doing.
